newsitem.title: CHINA: China bank and ministry to share dam loan risk.
newsitem.headline: China bank and ministry to share dam loan risk.

text.p: China's State Development Bank and Ministry of Water Resources have agreed to share the risk of $109 million in foreign government credit and bank loans for a major dam project, the China Daily said on Friday.

Construction of the Xiaolangdi water control project in central Henan province was being stepped up and the dam's first generating unit was scheduled to begin operating at the end of 1997, the newspaper said.
The development bank and water ministry on Thursday signed an agreement to share loan risk for importing the dam's electrical equipment, it said.
A tender would soon be issued for the equipment, it said, but gave no details.
Purchase of the dam's generating equipment had already been agreed with U.S. firm Voith Hydro Inc, it said.

State media last year reported that the U.S. Export-Import Bank had approved financing for part of a $58 million sale of turbines, accessories and services by Voith Hydro to the dam, which will be the biggest on China's northern Yellow River.
